verses.text: After that, Jesus crossed to the far side of the Sea of Galilee, aka the Sea of Tiberias.
A massive crowd was trailing him, because they’d seen the signs he did for sick people.
Jesus headed up the hillside and sat down there with his disciples. 🌄
Passover, the Jewish festival, was coming up.
Jesus looked up, saw the crowd coming his way, and asked Philip, “Where are we supposed to buy bread for all these people?”
He was putting Philip on the spot, but Jesus already knew what he was about to do.
Philip answered, “Even two hundred denarii worth of bread wouldn’t give everyone more than a little bite.”
Andrew, one of the disciples and Simon Peter’s brother, jumped in:
“There’s a kid here with five barley loaves and two fish. But come on, what’s that for this whole crowd?”
Jesus said, “Have everybody sit down.” There was loads of grass there, so the men settled in—about five thousand of them.
Jesus took the loaves and gave thanks. Then he handed them to his disciples to pass around. He did the same with the fish, giving everyone as much as they wanted.
When everybody had eaten their fill, Jesus told his disciples, “Gather up the leftovers. Don’t let anything go to waste.”
They scooped up the leftovers and filled twelve baskets with pieces from the five barley loaves the crowd had eaten. 🍞
When the people saw the sign Jesus had done, they said, “This really is the Prophet who was coming into the world!”
Jesus knew they were about to grab him and make him king by force, so he slipped back up the hillside alone.
When evening came, the disciples headed down to the sea.
They got into a boat and set off across the sea for Capernaum. It was dark, and Jesus still hadn’t joined them.
A strong wind kicked up, and the water got rough. 🌊
After rowing about three or four miles, they spotted Jesus walking on the sea and coming toward the boat. Fear hit them.
But he said, “It’s me. Don’t be scared.”
They welcomed him into the boat, and right away they reached the shore they were headed for.
Next day, the crowd still across the sea clocked that there had only been one boat. They knew Jesus hadn’t left with his disciples in it; the disciples had gone alone.
Some boats from Tiberias landed near the spot where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord gave thanks.
When the crowd realized Jesus and his disciples weren’t there, they hopped into the boats and went looking for him in Capernaum.
They found him across the sea and asked, “Rabbi, when did you get here?”
Jesus answered, “Real talk: you’re looking for me because you ate the loaves and got full, not because you saw the signs.
Don’t burn your energy chasing food that spoils. Work for the food that lasts into eternal life—the Son of Man will give it to you. God the Father has put his seal on him.”
They asked him, “So what should we do to carry out God’s work?”
Jesus answered, “Here’s God’s work for you: believe in the one he sent.”
They said, “Then what sign are you doing so we can see it and believe you? What work are you doing?
Our ancestors ate manna in the wilderness. Scripture says, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
Jesus told them, “I’m telling you straight: Moses didn’t give you the bread from heaven. My Father is the one giving you the true bread from heaven.
God’s bread is the one coming down from heaven and giving life to the world.”
They said, “Lord, keep that bread coming.”
Jesus told them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me won’t go hungry; whoever believes in me won’t be thirsty again.” 💛
But I’ve told you already: you’ve seen me, and you still don’t believe.
Everyone the Father gives me will come to me. Anyone who comes to me, I’ll never turn away—no way.
I came down from heaven to do my Father’s will, not to run my own agenda.
This is what my Father wants: I must not lose any of those he gave me; I’ll raise them up on the last day.
My Father wants everyone who sees the Son and believes in him to have eternal life. I’ll raise them up on the last day.”
The Jewish leaders started grumbling about Jesus because he said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
They said, “Isn’t that Jesus, Joseph’s son? We know his parents. So how’s he claiming he came down from heaven?”
Jesus answered, “Quit grumbling among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them. I’ll raise them up on the last day.
The prophets wrote, ‘They’ll all be taught by God.’ Everyone who listens to the Father and learns from him comes to me.
No one has seen the Father except the one who comes from God. He has seen the Father.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness—and they died.
But here’s the bread coming down from heaven, so anyone can eat it and not die.
I am the living bread from heaven. Anyone who eats this bread will live forever. The bread I give for the world’s life is my flesh.”
The Jewish leaders started arguing with each other: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I’ll raise them up on the last day.
My flesh is real food, and my blood is real drink—straight up.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood stays in me, and I stay in them.
The living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father. In the same way, whoever feeds on me will live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven. It’s not like the manna your ancestors ate and then died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.”
Jesus said all this while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.
A lot of his disciples heard him and said, “This teaching is tough. Who can even take it in?”
Jesus knew his disciples were grumbling about it. He asked, “Does this trip you up?
Then what if you saw the Son of Man going up to where he was before?
The Spirit is the one who gives life; the flesh gets you nowhere. The words I’ve spoken to you are spirit and life.
But some of you don’t believe.” Jesus knew from the start who didn’t believe and who would betray him.
He added, “That’s why I told you no one can come to me unless my Father grants it to them.”
After that, many disciples backed out and stopped following Jesus. 🚶
Jesus asked the Twelve, “You don’t want to leave too, do you?”
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, who else are we going to? You have the words of eternal life.
We’ve come to believe and know you’re the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered them, “I chose you, all twelve, didn’t I? And one of you is a devil.”
Jesus was talking about Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son. Judas was one of the Twelve, but he was going to betray Jesus.
